post.description:
Records an already-collected offline donation (cash, bank transfer,
etc.) without going through a payment gateway. Staff-only: online
donations from the public must use POST /donations/checkout + /verify,
which actually verify payment before marking a donation SUCCESS.

Create a PENDING donation plus a payment-provider order. The client
opens the provider's checkout with the returned order details, then calls
`/donations/verify` once the user completes payment.

Reconcile a single successful donation into the finance ledger.

The app calls this per-donation; the bulk flow remains available at
POST /finance/reconcile/donations. Delegates to the finance domain
service so the reconciliation transaction/ledger rules stay in one place.

get.description: Public listing of currently accepting donation campaigns.

post.description:
A potential owner submits verification documents against a match. Only
the reporters of either side of the match may claim it (PRR 3.10).

Staff verifies a submitted claim. Approval confirms the match and
resolves both reports; rejection marks the match rejected. The reviewer
and time are captured in the audit trail.

Confirmation from the SENDING facility. A transfer only completes
once both this and /confirm-receiver have been called (PRR 3.6).

Confirmation from the RECEIVING facility. A transfer only completes
once both this and /confirm-sender have been called (PRR 3.6).

AdoptionStatus.title: AdoptionStatus
AdoptionStatus.description:
Six-phase adoption pipeline (PRR 3.7) plus a terminal REJECTED.

SUBMITTED -> SCREENING -> INTERVIEW -> HOME_CHECK -> APPROVED -> COMPLETED.

``VETTING`` is a deprecated legacy member kept only so historical rows
that stored the collapsed ``"vetting"`` value (the old phases 1+2) still
parse. It is NOT part of the active state machine and has no valid
transitions; new applications use SCREENING/INTERVIEW.

RescueFailureReason.title: RescueFailureReason
RescueFailureReason.description:
Standardized outcome codes for failed rescues (PRR 3.3).

Field agents must log one of these codes instead of free text so failure
analytics (Rescue Operational Efficiency Report) can group by a bounded
set. Legacy free-text values are normalised to these codes by the API
layer and the backfill migration.

RescuePhysicalCondition.title: RescuePhysicalCondition
RescuePhysicalCondition.description:
Controlled physical-condition categories per PRR 3.2 intake payload.

Legacy free-text values (e.g. "Injured", "Critical") are normalised to
these canonical values by the API schema and the backfill migration, so
dashboards and reports can group by a stable, bounded set.

RescueSeverity.title: RescueSeverity
RescueSeverity.description:
Operational priority for a rescue case (PRR 3.2 severity prioritization).

CRITICAL/HIGH cases feed the public urgent-alert banner (PRR 3.1.1) and the
coordinator dispatch queue; the explicit `is_urgent` flag on the request
lets coordinators surface a case for community assistance regardless of
its severity label.
